entries.title: Tag your articles, privately, and filter by them
entries.body: You can give articles your own tags, from the Tag button on each card or row in your library, or the tag box near the top of an article's Metadata page. Only you see them. Once you have tags, a Tags row appears above Topics; pick several tags and topics and your library narrows to the articles that match them all. Exports include an article's tags.

entries.title: Highlight passages in four colours
entries.body: When you select words to comment on, you can give them a yellow, green, blue or pink highlight, and change the colour later from the comment. A highlight with no note, and the AI not asked, is kept as a plain highlight: it shows in the text and in your list of comments, with no note in the margin. Where highlights overlap, the newest one sets the colour and is the one a click opens.

entries.title: Modes are told to skip an article's paperwork
entries.body: The AI behind Sketch, Illustrated, FAQ, Quiz, Ideas, Quotes, Glossary, Timeline and Debate is now told to pass over passages that only say what the piece is, or how it was produced, published and sourced. Evidence, reasoning, method and limitations still count. Results you already have mostly change only when they are made again.

entries.title: Paragraph icons move to the text's right
entries.body: The small icons beside each paragraph and heading (link, comment, ? and …) and the reading-time line now sit to the right of the article rather than the left. On wide screens the icons and the article's title also line up more closely with the text, where they had drifted out of line.

entries.title: Where a section sits, and how much you've read
entries.body: Point at or tap a section on the strip showing where you are, and its card shows where it sits in the article's outline: its part, the sections around it, and its own sub-sections. In Quiz, the share of the piece you have read is drawn as a small pie; point at or tap it for the figure.

entries.title: The Glossary button moves to the panel's top
entries.body: The button that finds terms is the first thing in the Glossary panel, and says Find more when it will add to your list, or Find terms again when it will replace it. On an article's Metadata page, pressing Metadata again (or Cmd/Ctrl-Enter) takes you back to the article; it used to do nothing.

entries.title: Tap to talk when a conversation stalls
entries.body: When you talk to an article out loud, background voices can keep it waiting for you to finish speaking. The notice that appears then offers Tap to talk: press Talk, speak, press Done, and the reply follows. It stays on for the rest of that call, Reconnect included; hands-free calls are otherwise unchanged.

entries.title: Cards open with a tap on touch screens
entries.body: On a phone or tablet, the cards in Structure and on the reading-time line beside each paragraph did not open at all. A tap opens them now; in Structure a second tap takes you there, and rows without a card still go straight there. Citations cards opened by a tap close when you scroll.
